# mpd-dsh bundle plugin layer (Plan D): ADDITIVE-ONLY patch, plus TWO id-targets
# (the two preset-roster rows below: `agent-presets` on the web/base plane and
# `dsh-tui-agent-presets` on the dsh-tui plane — each exists in exactly ONE
# composition, so neither target can ever duplicate the other's loader entry id).
# Policy: never id-target rows owned by the stock DSH templates (llm-deepseek /
# agent-default-model / skill-filesystem / llm-pi-ai) — id-target replaces the
# WHOLE stock config and would wipe the stock model list / provider defaults.
# DeepSeek official provider ships with dsh-base as-is; this bundle adds only:
# MCP servers, the mpd-* plugins, the adopted agent-teams plugin, and the
# bundle-served preset root (the skill corpus is served by the mpd-bootstrap
# row's ctx.skills provider — nothing is copied into $DSH_HOME any more).

# ── preset roster: serve the bundle's own presets (no $DSH_HOME copy) ───────
# The bundle ships its presets at <bundle>/presets and serves them from there by
# adding a `system`-trust root, so ONE `dsh plugin add` makes the mpd preset
# selectable and ONE `dsh plugin remove` takes it away with the bundle — no
# $DSH_HOME/.agent-presets copy, no stale-copy refresh dance.
#
# This is an id-target (replace), not an insert: dsh-web-app's own patch already
# inserts this row with `default: standard`, and a second insert would be a
# duplicate loader entry id (fatal at boot). The stock row's whole config is
# exactly `default` — its own comment says "This row only names the default and
# any deployment-added roots" — so restating it here is complete, and both keys
# are required to keep the roster working.
#
# Profiles WITHOUT the row (headless) log "patch: entry agent-presets not found"
# and skip it: headless never had a preset roster, so nothing regresses.
- id: agent-presets
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
  config:
    default: mpd
    roots:
      - path: !!js '(typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/presets"'
        trust: system

# ── preset roster, dsh-tui plane: the same default, for the TUI composition ──
# MEASURED (2026-09-15, dsh-tui@0.10.1 + engine 0.1.5-rc.2, isolated sandbox):
# the id-target above is SKIPPED in a dsh-tui profile, because no layer of that
# composition inserts an `agent-presets` row — dsh-web-app owns it, and dsh-tui
# does not use that layer. The TUI's own roster row carries the scoped id
# `dsh-tui-agent-presets` (name `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets`, config
# `{ default: 'standard' }`, `disabled: <an enabled `agent-presets` entry
# exists>`), so a live session recorded `agentPreset: "standard"` — user
# decision D10 ("TUI sessions must default to the mpd preset") was NOT satisfied
# by the web-plane row alone.
#
# This id-target replaces that row's WHOLE config (loader semantics), so the
# stock config is restated: `default: mpd` plus the bundle's own preset root —
# exactly the same two keys the web-plane row above declares. The stock
# expression's other branch (a fallback root for legacy packages that ship NO
# bundled `presets/` directory) is deliberately NOT restated: the validated pin
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets@0.1.5-rc.2` ships `presets/{standard,ptc,
# cordis,minimal}`, so that branch is dead here, and re-adding the dsh CLI's own
# preset directory as a second root would shadow preset ids the package already
# serves. Its `disabled` expression is left untouched (no override), so the row
# stays enabled in a dsh-tui composition.
#
# Safety of the pair: each row exists in exactly one composition (the TUI row is
# minted by dsh-tui's own patch, the plain row by dsh-web-app's), so the other
# profile only logs `patch: entry <id> not found` and applies nothing — no
# duplicate loader entry id is possible in either. Loader semantics that make the
# pair safe and this id-target complete: an id-target is a per-key shallow
# override (cordis-plugin-include src/index.ts:120-124 assigns only the keys this
# file carries and skips `id`), so the host row's own `disabled` expression
# survives; a missing id-target is a WARN (same file, :112), never an error; a
# duplicate entry id is fatal (cordis-plugin-loader src/config/group.ts:64).
#
# Evidence, split by claim — every citation names an artifact that exists AND says
# what it proves (a `--dump-config` file proves COMPOSITION only, never a load):
#  • D10 (a TUI session really ran the mpd preset) — SESSION RECORDS, shipped as
#    durable byte-identical copies inside this bundle's own evidence dir (sha256
#    asserted equal to the sandbox original; every record, relied-upon or not, is
#    indexed in evidence/tui/composition/20260915T053445Z/raw/session-records-index.json):
#      · evidence/tui/composition/20260915T053445Z/raw/sessions/--root-dshProj-my-power-dsh--/
#        683c0f89-d2ea-4bf1-817e-3593eb765441/session.v3.jsonl.zstd
#        sha256 d78ddb81aafad905ba8085db6f86d64807f5043ddadb884f39337c9f9e147689 — agentPreset "mpd"
#        (concatenated-zstd frames, header line `{"type":"session",…,"agentPreset":"mpd"}`)
#      · the same directory holds a9eea0a3-aa4e-45e2-8d4d-3856b0b606d1
#        (sha256 225152d4eb4bb04c037b9d455562d8af03c136a898ea287d37fb9f5c958c8763) and
#        c7f6db60-5246-4223-9b2c-ad38ac87eea6
#        (sha256 4471a31dab863c1fda8733de49bb29e3edaa2ec61e0366e08077780409671f03), each "mpd".
#    The CONTRAST ships beside them: the same-shaped records from BEFORE this id-target
#    existed, each recording `agentPreset: "standard"` — the measured "before" this fix
#    answers (de5fde53-…/sha256 0e67008c…, 1a5d7e6f-…/ff7954b5…, e11887f7-…/6f3e02ec…,
#    all three in the index).
#  • The web profile is unchanged — a COMPOSITION check only:
#    evidence/tui/composition/20260915T053445Z/raw/web-dump-config.err (its sole
#    warning is `patch: entry "dsh-tui-agent-presets" not found`) and
#    …/raw/web-dump-config.txt (exactly ONE @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets row).
#    The BOOT proof for that profile is the bundle-lifecycle mounting boot (R6,
#    `bun skills/dsh-qa/scripts/bundle-lifecycle.mjs`), which really mounts the web
#    profile — never a `--dump-config` result, which only composes rows (AGENTS.md §4).
- id: dsh-tui-agent-presets
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
  config:
    default: mpd
    roots:
      - path: !!js '(typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/presets"'
        trust: system

# ── runtime plugin dependency: the sidebar HOST the bundle's GUI needs ──────
# MEASURED DEFECT (evidence/install-deps/red-baseline/20260920T030832Z/result.json):
# a clean install of this bundle alone composed ZERO `dsh-better-sidebar` rows, so
# the `betterSidebar` service never existed and the bundle's two sidebar pages
# (mpd-agent-teams, mpd-workmate) registered nothing — the reported "the sidebar
# cannot display". The package is declared in the bundle manifest's `dependencies`
# (dsh-better-sidebar 0.19.0-alpha.1) and MOUNTED here.
#
# BOTH halves are required. The declaration alone never mounts anything: `dsh plugin
# add` reconciles only PROFILE-level dependencies into `dsh.profile.bundles`, so a
# bundle's dependency never becomes a layer and the package's own guarded patch never
# applies. The row alone would be boot-fatal when the module is unresolvable
# (`assertEntriesLoaded`). What makes the row resolvable is
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot#healProfileModuleFallback`, which materializes the
# dependency closure of every non-installation bundle layer into
# `<profile>/node_modules` before the loader runs (measured; see the ledger under
# evidence/install-deps/implementation/**).
#
# THE ENTRY ID IS DELIBERATELY `mpd-better-sidebar`, byte-different from the
# package's own patch id (`better-sidebar`) and from the aggregate's id
# (`web-ui-better-sidebar`, @linxin666/dsh-web-all): a duplicate loader ENTRY ID is
# fatal even when the guard would have disabled one of the two, so we never reuse an
# id another layer may mint.
#
# THE GUARD IS ORDER-INDEPENDENT — the property that makes BOTH install orders safe.
# `[...ctx.loader.entries()]` is FORWARD-BLIND at first evaluation (measured: the
# same expression re-evaluates later with every entry visible, but `Entry.refresh()`
# returns early once `this.fiber` exists, so the FIRST evaluation decides), and
# @linxin666/dsh-web-all mounts the sidebar with an UNGUARDED row. A guard that read
# only the entry list would kill a boot that works today whenever the aggregate is
# installed AFTER this bundle. So the guard reads DECLARATIONS instead:
#   1. no `dsh-better-sidebar` resolvable from `<profile>/node_modules` -> disable
#      (degrade to "no sidebar" with one warning, never fail the boot);
#   2. `dsh-better-sidebar` is itself a declared `dsh.profile.bundles` layer -> its
#      own patch mounts it -> disable;
#   3. every OTHER bundle layer's `dsh.bundle.patch` text names the package -> disable.
#      Self-exclusion is by IDENTITY (the layer whose `package.json` name is
#      `@mpd-dsh/mpd` is SKIPPED), never by a substring of our own row id: a foreign
#      layer that mounts the package while merely mentioning `mpd-better-sidebar` in a
#      comment must still be detected (review R4);
#   4. EVERY other patch layer the loader composes is scanned the same way (review R1):
#      `<profileDir>/cordis.patch.yml`, `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`
#      (`<profileDir>/../../cordis.patch.yml`) and every `--patch` overlay path
#      recovered from `process.argv` (both `--patch X` and `--patch=X`, repeatable).
#      A sidebar row in any of them under a DIFFERENT entry id is exactly the
#      `duplicate prefix route` boot-killer (requirements F3) and is now seen;
#   5. no enabled `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` ENTRY -> disable. The web-plane
#      clause is fail-closed (review R3): the raw `options.disabled` node must be
#      absent or literally `false`, so a webserver row disabled by an expression is NOT
#      "present", and the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` layer no longer enables this row on
#      its own — the service the sidebar injects is the entry's, not the layer's.
# OVER-APPROXIMATION IS DELIBERATE: a layer that merely MENTIONS `dsh-better-sidebar`
# in a comment disables this row. A false disable costs the sidebar (one log line, the
# session keeps running); a false enable kills the whole boot with `webserver: duplicate
# route`. When in doubt this guard disables.
# The whole guard is one try/catch that returns TRUE (disabled) on ANY throw, so the
# worst case is a missing sidebar, never a dead boot. It logs ONE line per distinct
# decision with the stable prefix `[mpd-better-sidebar] mount guard: ` — that line is
# how a verifier sees the decision in the boot log. Raw `e.options.disabled` is read
# on purpose: reading another entry's EVALUATED `disabled` getter re-enters its own
# `!!js` expression (measured: mutual recursion, stack overflow).

- insert:
    # B8 (wave 2): this row names NO binary path any more. It launches
    # packages/mpd-mcp-astgrep/launch.mjs, which resolves the binary
    # bundle-relatively (env pin -> $MPD_AST_GREP_BIN_DIR -> createRequire of the
    # optionalDependency -> <bundle>/.toolchain/node_modules/.bin/ast-grep|sg) and
    # sets MPD_AST_GREP_SG_PATH only when the caller left it unset, before the
    # adopted server reads it. The old `env.MPD_AST_GREP_SG_PATH = <baseUrl>/node_modules/.bin/sg`
    # pin was packed-layout-only AND named the deprecated `sg` wrapper (exit 1);
    # a mounting boot with no env pin is the gate (never `--dump-config`).
    - id: mcp-astgrep
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: ast_grep
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_ASTGREP_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-astgrep/launch.mjs")'
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
    # git_bash, by the upstream original design, is Windows-only (run is available only on native Windows); this bundle disables it by default;
    # Windows deployments can change this row to disabled: false to enable it.
    - id: mcp-gitbash
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      disabled: true
      config:
        serverName: git_bash
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_GITBASH_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-gitbash/dist/cli.js")'
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
    - id: mcp-lsp
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: lsp
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_LSP_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-lsp/dist/cli.js")'
          - mcp
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
    # CodeGraph MCP (B8, wave 2): this row names NO binary path any more. It
    # launches packages/mpd-mcp-codegraph/launch.mjs, which resolves the binary
    # bundle-relatively (env pin -> createRequire of the optionalDependency ->
    # <bundle>/.toolchain/node_modules/.bin/codegraph) and sets MPD_CODEGRAPH_BIN
    # only when the caller left it unset, then calls runCodegraphServe() (serve.js
    # self-starts only when IT is argv[1]). The old env pin was packed-layout-only,
    # and a wrong MPD_CODEGRAPH_BIN disables the adopted bundled/provisioned/PATH/
    # download chain entirely. Project index init/skip-home discipline is handled
    # by the mpd-codegraph plugin row below.
    - id: mcp-codegraph
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: codegraph
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_CODEGRAPH_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-codegraph/launch.mjs")'
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
    # Waveform-read MCP rows (mcp-wave-mcp / mcp-traceweave) are NOT mounted by
    # default: they wrap EXTERNAL Python MCP servers (wave-mcp / TraceWeave)
    # that the user installs with pipx or plain pip — NO venv required (the
    # venv iron rule belongs to cocotb only; pipx keeps the two tools isolated
    # on its own if their mcp SDK versions ever conflict). A missing or
    # mismatched mcp SDK on the launching python crashed the MCP client at boot
    # (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp.server.mcpserver'), taking the
    # whole GUI/agent down → boot-safety rule: optional rows stay COMMENTED
    # until the tools are installed and the env bins are pinned. To enable:
    #   1) pipx install wave-mcp && pipx install traceweave-mcp
    #      (or run node scripts/install-mcp.mjs --with-wave --activate-wave)
    #   2) export MPD_DSH_WAVE_MCP_BIN=$(command -v wave-mcp)
    #      export MPD_DSH_TRACEWEAVE_BIN=$(command -v traceweave-mcp)
    #   3) uncomment the two example rows below (command resolves env-first,
    #      PATH second).
    # - id: mcp-wave-mcp
    #   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
    #   config:
    #     serverName: wave_mcp
    #     transport: stdio
    #     command: !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_WAVE_MCP_BIN || "wave-mcp"'
    #     # NO --session at startup: wave-mcp 0.1.1 treats --session as an
    #     # OPTIONAL auto-open and exits with FileNotFoundError when the dir has
    #     # no session.json yet. The plugin creates the session after a sim run
    #     # via mcp__wave_mcp__prepare_session.
    #     toolCallTimeoutMs: 120000
    # - id: mcp-traceweave
    #   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
    #   config:
    #     serverName: traceweave
    #     transport: stdio
    #     command: !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_TRACEWEAVE_BIN || "traceweave-mcp"'
    #     # No env block: the EDA environment (VERDI_HOME/NOVAS_HOME/VCS_HOME +
    #     # license vars) is inherited from the dsh launching shell; docs instruct
    #     # exporting them there before starting dsh.
    #     toolCallTimeoutMs: 120000

# ── B-line plugins (self-written; production uses @mpd-dsh/<pkg> package names) ──
- insert:
    # Web-compat self-registration (mirrors @linxin666/dsh-web-ui-all's web-ui-compat
    # row): the bundle's web client loads only if a LOADER ENTRY named exactly
    # `@mpd-dsh/mpd` exists — client-modules resolves client rows against
    # `ctx.loader.entries()` entry names, and entry names come from a patch row's
    # `name` field. This self-row (loading the bundle's own no-op main plugin)
    # provides that entry; without it the agent-teams/workmate web client never
    # appears in the boot graph.
    - id: mpd-web-compat
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd'
    # mpd-dsh-adapter FIRST: it is the bundle's ONLY contact surface with the
    # harness tool/agent/skill/preset seams (ctx.tools register/guard/execute/
    # post-execute, ctx.subagents.start, ctx.skills.registerProvider,
    # ctx.agentPresets.resolve). Every mpd row below calls through it, so a
    # harness release that reshapes a seam is absorbed in that one package.
    - id: mpd-dsh-adapter
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # mpd-config next: it provides the mpdConfig service that the rows below
    # read (apply-time config merges for tools/waterfalls).
    - id: mpd-config
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-config-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # Team watchdog (w3 core): per-step/per-tool heartbeat store for members AND the
    # captain, the configurable WARN→ESCALATE machine over the `mpd` namespace's
    # watchdog.* knobs, the atomic restorable scene snapshot, and the durable
    # watchdogHold + incident/read-watermark sidecars written BESIDE the adopted
    # `team.json` (that record keeps its single writer, state.js). It owns its own
    # `session-watchdog-hold`/`-resume` actions; wiring the adopted dispatch gates
    # that honour a hold is a later task, so this row registers the contract only.
    # HOST plane on purpose: a preset row's listeners are scoped to one agent, so a
    # preset-mounted tick could not witness a wedged CAPTAIN (AC-9).
    - id: mpd-team-watchdog
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-team-watchdog-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        # The ROW layer of the T-18 three-layer defaults table: every value here must equal
        # `packages/mpd-team-watchdog-plugin/src/machine.ts` `WATCHDOG_DEFAULTS` and
        # `packages/mpd-config-plugin/src/settings-schema.ts` `SettingsSchema.watchdog`. A
        # composition that writes no `watchdog` section in the `mpd` namespace keeps these.
        # A settings edit reaches the RUNNING engine only through the settings-document
        # re-read (`engine.ts` `onSettingsDocumentUpdated`); a `.mpd/mpd.jsonc` edit is read
        # once at plugin mount, so it applies at the next dsh boot and never mid-process.
        stateDir: '.mpd/team'
        warnSilenceMs: 600000
        tickIntervalMs: 15000
        warnStreakToEscalate: 6
        actionOnEscalate: warn-only
        toolInFlightMaxMs: 900000
        holdTtlMs: 900000
    - id: mpd-tools
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-tools-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        writeGuard: true
        truncateMaxBytes: 8192
    - id: mpd-modelchain
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-modelchain-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # mpd-ext: the extension registry — it provides the `mpdExtensions` service and the
    # four model-facing tools (mpd_ext_list / mpd_ext_show / mpd_flow_list / mpd_flow_show).
    # POSITION (bundle-patch change, plan [REV3] §1.4): after mpd-dsh-adapter and mpd-config,
    # directly above mpd-roles — its first consumer. Row order is deliberately NOT the
    # dependency mechanism here (docs/design.md: a sibling-provided service is read
    # lazily at tool-execute time; the dependency mechanism that exists is `inject`), so the
    # row works anywhere in this band and the band documents the intended direction:
    #   · ABOVE mpd-dsh-adapter the row's apply-time `ctx.get("mpdDsh")` finds no mounted
    #     adapter and takes the `?? createDshAdapter(ctx)` fallback — the hazard, and the fix
    #     for it, are described ONCE in the canonical note at
    #     packages/mpd-ext-plugin/src/index.ts (resolveAdapter) and are NOT restated here; this
    #     bullet only states the placement rule. The branch now warns once per apply
    #     (`adapterIdentity=fallback:createDshAdapter`) instead of staying silent, so a
    #     misordered composition is visible in a boot log.
    #   · BELOW mpd-roles inverts the direction: today mpd-roles resolves the service with a
    #     per-call `ctx.get("mpdExtensions")`, but any later conversion of that lazy get into
    #     a hard `inject: ["mpdExtensions"]` would make mpd-roles a FATAL `pending` loader
    #     entry (the measured class that takes the whole plugin tree down) AND lose every
    #     extension-contributed role, because the provider row applies after its consumer.
    # `quiet` is the plugin's ONLY config key (MpdExtPluginConfig); false keeps the one-line
    # apply summary.
    - id: mpd-ext
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-ext-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        quiet: false
    - id: mpd-roles
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-roles-plugin/dist/index.js'
    - id: mpd-ulw
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-ulw-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        maxRounds: 3
    - id: mpd-hashline
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-hashline-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        guardEditTools: true
    - id: mpd-boulder
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-boulder-plugin/dist/index.js'
    - id: mpd-comment-checker
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-comment-checker-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        autoCheck: false
    - id: mpd-codegraph
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-codegraph-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        autoInit: true
        initTimeoutMs: 60000
    - id: mpd-memory
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-memory-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        vcs: git
    - id: mpd-workmate
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # Compacts a FINISHED team's members (every task terminal AND every member idle).
    # Members only — the captain is compacted by the human /compact command. The engine is
    # resolved per member through that member's OWN scoped context; the host-plane engine is
    # a different object serving a different realm (measured: sameObject false), so the
    # lookup lives in ONE adapter helper. Audit lands under <workspace>/.mpd/team-compact/;
    # this row never writes .mpd/team (that state belongs to the agent-teams plugin).
    - id: mpd-team-compact
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-team-compact-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # Bundle asset provisioning (no home writes since 0.3.0): registers the
    # <bundle>/skills corpus as a ctx.skills provider (rank 600 "bundled", below
    # project/custom/user roots) and removes the version-stamped copies that
    # bundle <= 0.2.6 left in $DSH_HOME/skills + $DSH_HOME/.agent-presets.
    # The preset side is served by the agent-presets row at the top of this file.
    - id: mpd-bootstrap
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-bootstrap-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # DSH-TUI edition (D1/D2/D6/D10): the TUI-native surface package for this
    # bundle. It binds the host's activation-gated UI service seams (tuiStatus,
    # tuiRenderers, tuiSettingsSections, tuiScenes, tuiCommandTrees,
    # tuiShortcuts, tuiDialogs) and probes every one of them with
    # `ctx.get(id, false)` + warn-once degrade, so under a profile that provides
    # none of them (web/headless) the row degrades instead of taking the boot
    # down. The same package's admission facet is declared ONCE, bundle-level, by
    # dsh-plugin.json at the repo root (`facets.host.entry` = the module below);
    # the package ships NO cordis.patch.yml of its own, so this row is the only
    # mount and no composition can duplicate the `mpd-tui` loader entry id
    # (verify-rows-parity + the boot-log scan are the gates).
    - id: mpd-tui
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-tui-plugin/dist/index.js'

# ── Remote MCP rows (public services; network required, optional per use) ──
- insert:
    # The adopted team plugin is FIRST-CLASS MAIN CODE at
    # packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin (MIT provenance; upstream
    # @nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams 0.1.16-rc.3-mpd) and loads through the bundle exports map:
    # pnpm-driven `dsh plugin add` never links a bundle's transitive dependencies
    # into the profile root, so a plain package-name row would silently self-disable.
    # Its server runtime closure is vendored at packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/_deps
    # (see scripts/vendor-agent-teams.mjs), so the row always resolves — no guard.
    - id: agent-teams
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/index.js'
      config:
        stateDir: .mpd/team
        memberProvider: spawn
        memberMaxDepth: 1
        maxMembers: 16
        # CONFIGURATION PLANE (goal 4): aligned to upstream team_mode
        # (packages/team-core/src/config.ts:6-14) with the user's decision that
        # OUR ceilings stay the more permissive local values. `enforcement`
        # mirrors upstream ('enforce' blocks over-limit sends, 'observe' logs
        # only; default enforce). Every key is absent-safe: a profile without
        # them still boots on these defaults.
        maxParallelMembers: 8
        maxMessagesPerRun: 10000
        maxWallClockMinutes: 120
        maxMemberTurns: 500
        messagePayloadMaxBytes: 32768
        recipientUnreadMaxBytes: 262144
        mailboxPollIntervalMs: 3000
        enforcement: enforce
        # R3: empty staged teams older than this are ARCHIVED at the next session
        # start (never deleted), excluding the running session's own team.
        reclaimStaleAfterMs: 3600000
        # SESSION-START TEAM GATE (binding): a session starts with NO team — a
        # team is NOT a precondition. mode=off is the default (upstream parity:
        # team_mode.enabled defaults to false) and means "no auto-provision, no
        # unconditional notice". The DECOUPLED mechanical gate is `autoRoute`
        # (default enabled): at the session's first pre-step it evaluates the
        # frozen complexity gate, whose predicate is
        #   trigger = explicit flag OR (matchedSignals >= 1)
        # with signals A (a `team:` prefix or `!team`, the marker is consumed),
        # B (>=4 distinct deliverable verbs), C (>=3 enumerated lines / action
        # verbs / clauses) and D (a `.mpd/plans/*.md` artifact exists).
        # A triggered SOFT signal is ADVISORY: NOTHING is staged (no team state
        # is created) — the plugin injects ONE advisory notice that names the
        # fired signals, states that no team was staged, and tells the captain to
        # stage one on demand with agent_teams_create(approval="required",
        # profile="mpd") at the moment the work actually warrants a team
        # (otherwise continue solo and say so). An explicit `team:` / `!team`
        # request still PROVISIONS the staged default team (profile `mpd`,
        # approval=required — nothing spawns until the user approves the Web
        # plan), and mode=auto keeps the legacy unconditional provisioning as an
        # explicit opt-in; mode=instruct keeps the legacy instruction notice.
        # presets: [mpd] scopes the gate to mpd-preset sessions (sessions without
        # any preset, e.g. headless direct runs, are covered too), and
        # subagent/member sessions (they carry parentSession) never qualify. The
        # gate runs on the PRE-STEP, before any sizing doctrine, so it can
        # actually prevent a team.
        sessionTeamPolicy:
          mode: off
          autoRoute: true
          profile: mpd
          presets:
            - mpd
          name: MPD Default
          approval: required
        # The specialists become teammate instantiation templates for the
        # adopted dsh-agent-teams plugin (reusing its architecture + Web GUI).
        # One named profile `mpd` holds the full normal-named roster and
        # `taskPlanning: captain` means only the roster is fixed: the captain
        # designs the task DAG after a staged plan the user reviews in the panel.
        # /agent-teams --profile mpd <goal> instantiates the roster explicitly.
        profiles:
          mpd:
            description: "The specialist roster surfaced as normal-named teammate templates — captain-planned (roster only; the captain designs the DAG during the staged plan)."
            protocol: "Read-only members (Architect, Researcher, Planner, Explorer, Plan Reviewer, Vision Analyst) take requirements/review/analysis tasks only and never edit files. Workers (Senior Engineer, Junior Engineer, Deep Worker, Lead, Reviewer) take implementation/verification/integration. The captain leads, designs the DAG, and integrates results. Workmate reuse: before delegating a role task, consult mpd_workmate_list / mpd_workmate_match(task); if a workmate note matches well, delegate to that workmate (member name = workmate name, so its persona/memory are injected), otherwise initialize a fresh workmate with mpd_workmate_init — never force a weak note match."
            taskPlanning: captain
            # fallback.provider is ALWAYS deepseek-official (never the bare
            # "deepseek" compat-track provider): the original layered design
            # intended dsh-llm-pi-ai ("deepseek") as the degradation tier, but
            # that row is OFF by default (install-profile --with-compat-track is
            # gone) and the harness only registers deepseek-official
            # (dsh-llm-deepseek), so a "deepseek" fallback would fail with
            # NO_ADAPTER exactly when the fallback is needed.
            # MEMBER ROUTES COME FROM THE SETTINGS SLOTS, not from literals: `tier: N` starts the
            # member on mpd.teamModels.slot<N> (provider + model + reasoning effort, editable in the
            # TUI /settings section and in the Web settings card). The frozen class mapping is
            # tier 1 = Architect/Planner/Reviewer/Lead/Senior Engineer, tier 2 = the analysts
            # (Researcher/Explorer/Plan Reviewer), tier 3 = the executors (Deep Worker/Junior
            # Engineer), tier 4 = the vision member (Vision Analyst). Slot 4's DEFAULT is Vision
            # Analyst's own vision route (deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp at `high`), so routing it
            # through the slot is behaviour-preserving while making its model configurable. A slot
            # edit applies at the next dsh boot, like every other mpd knob.
            members:
              - name: Architect
                tier: 1
                role: architecture review / deep debugging / self-review
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only architecture advisor. You advise, others execute — never edit files. Favor simplicity and existing patterns; give one clear recommendation with concise rationale and evidence."
                # Read-only members are MECHANICALLY restricted, not just instructed: these
                # names are the same seven the one-shot roster path denies
                # (mpd-roles-plugin / mpd-workmate-plugin READONLY_DENY), carried as profile
                # data because the adopted plugin cannot import across packages. Without
                # them a "read-only" member in a team kept write/edit/bash (measured
                # 2026-09-14: a member's own session ran `pwd` for real).

                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Researcher
                tier: 2
                role: code / open-source evidence search
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only researcher. Gather evidence from the codebase, AST/LSP and web sources; cite file:line and URLs; never edit files or invent findings."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Planner
                tier: 1
                role: planning / task decomposition
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only planner. Produce decision-complete, step-ordered plans with a checklist; never implement."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Explorer
                tier: 2
                role: read-only codebase exploration
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only explorer. Answer with evidence and absolute file paths; never edit files."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Reviewer
                tier: 1
                role: correctness / risk review
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Deep reviewer. Produce correctness/risk findings with evidence; recommend fixes but do not apply them."
              - name: Plan Reviewer
                tier: 2
                role: work-plan QA review / UI-UX critique
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only plan reviewer. Verify plans are executable and references valid; reject only true blockers; UI/UX critique only when explicitly asked; never edit files."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Vision Analyst
                tier: 4
                role: image / diagram analysis
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only vision analyst. Describe screenshots/diagrams precisely; never edit files or load anything by path."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Lead
                tier: 1
                role: orchestration / integration
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Orchestrator. Plan the macro structure, delegate independent units in parallel, integrate and verify results."
              - name: Deep Worker
                tier: 3
                role: autonomous goal-driven implementation
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Autonomous deep worker. Receive goals, execute them end-to-end with tools, verify every change, report evidence-first."
              - name: Senior Engineer
                tier: 1
                role: primary implementation
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Primary engineer. Plan small, execute with tools, keep diffs minimal, verify every change, report honestly."
              - name: Junior Engineer
                tier: 3
                role: small mechanical changes
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Fast executor. Small, well-scoped mechanical changes with quick verification; keep diffs tiny."

# `dsh-tui-agent-presets` on the dsh-tui plane — each exists in exactly ONE

# MCP servers, the mpd-* plugins, the adopted agent-teams plugin, and the

# row's ctx.skills provider — nothing is copied into $DSH_HOME any more).

# ── preset roster: serve the bundle's own presets (no $DSH_HOME copy) ───────
# The bundle ships its presets at <bundle>/presets and serves them from there by
# adding a `system`-trust root, so ONE `dsh plugin add` makes the mpd preset
# selectable and ONE `dsh plugin remove` takes it away with the bundle — no
# $DSH_HOME/.agent-presets copy, no stale-copy refresh dance.
#
# This is an id-target (replace), not an insert: dsh-web-app's own patch already
# inserts this row with `default: standard`, and a second insert would be a
# duplicate loader entry id (fatal at boot). The stock row's whole config is
# exactly `default` — its own comment says "This row only names the default and
# any deployment-added roots" — so restating it here is complete, and both keys
# are required to keep the roster working.
#
# Profiles WITHOUT the row (headless) log "patch: entry agent-presets not found"
# and skip it: headless never had a preset roster, so nothing regresses.

  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
  config:
    default: mpd
    roots:
      - path: !!js '(typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/presets"'
        trust: system

# the id-target above is SKIPPED in a dsh-tui profile, because no layer of that
# composition inserts an `agent-presets` row — dsh-web-app owns it, and dsh-tui
# does not use that layer. The TUI's own roster row carries the scoped id
# `dsh-tui-agent-presets` (name `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets`, config
# `{ default: 'standard' }`, `disabled: <an enabled `agent-presets` entry
# exists>`), so a live session recorded `agentPreset: "standard"` — user
# decision D10 ("TUI sessions must default to the mpd preset") was NOT satisfied
# by the web-plane row alone.

# This id-target replaces that row's WHOLE config (loader semantics), so the
# stock config is restated: `default: mpd` plus the bundle's own preset root —
# exactly the same two keys the web-plane row above declares. The stock
# expression's other branch (a fallback root for legacy packages that ship NO
# bundled `presets/` directory) is deliberately NOT restated: the validated pin

# preset directory as a second root would shadow preset ids the package already

# stays enabled in a dsh-tui composition.

# minted by dsh-tui's own patch, the plain row by dsh-web-app's), so the other

# ── runtime plugin dependency: the sidebar HOST the bundle's GUI needs ──────
# MEASURED DEFECT (evidence/install-deps/red-baseline/20260920T030832Z/result.json):
# a clean install of this bundle alone composed ZERO `dsh-better-sidebar` rows, so
# the `betterSidebar` service never existed and the bundle's two sidebar pages
# (mpd-agent-teams, mpd-workmate) registered nothing — the reported "the sidebar
# cannot display". The package is declared in the bundle manifest's `dependencies`
# (dsh-better-sidebar 0.19.0-alpha.1) and MOUNTED here.
#
# BOTH halves are required. The declaration alone never mounts anything: `dsh plugin
# add` reconciles only PROFILE-level dependencies into `dsh.profile.bundles`, so a
# bundle's dependency never becomes a layer and the package's own guarded patch never
# applies. The row alone would be boot-fatal when the module is unresolvable
# (`assertEntriesLoaded`). What makes the row resolvable is
# `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot#healProfileModuleFallback`, which materializes the
# dependency closure of every non-installation bundle layer into
# `<profile>/node_modules` before the loader runs (measured; see the ledger under
# evidence/install-deps/implementation/**).
#
# THE ENTRY ID IS DELIBERATELY `mpd-better-sidebar`, byte-different from the
# package's own patch id (`better-sidebar`) and from the aggregate's id
# (`web-ui-better-sidebar`, @linxin666/dsh-web-all): a duplicate loader ENTRY ID is
# fatal even when the guard would have disabled one of the two, so we never reuse an
# id another layer may mint.
#
# THE GUARD IS ORDER-INDEPENDENT — the property that makes BOTH install orders safe.
# `[...ctx.loader.entries()]` is FORWARD-BLIND at first evaluation (measured: the
# same expression re-evaluates later with every entry visible, but `Entry.refresh()`
# returns early once `this.fiber` exists, so the FIRST evaluation decides), and
# @linxin666/dsh-web-all mounts the sidebar with an UNGUARDED row. A guard that read
# only the entry list would kill a boot that works today whenever the aggregate is
# installed AFTER this bundle. So the guard reads DECLARATIONS instead:
#   1. no `dsh-better-sidebar` resolvable from `<profile>/node_modules` -> disable
#      (degrade to "no sidebar" with one warning, never fail the boot);
#   2. `dsh-better-sidebar` is itself a declared `dsh.profile.bundles` layer -> its
#      own patch mounts it -> disable;
#   3. every OTHER bundle layer's `dsh.bundle.patch` text names the package -> disable.
#      Self-exclusion is by IDENTITY (the layer whose `package.json` name is
#      `@mpd-dsh/mpd` is SKIPPED), never by a substring of our own row id: a foreign
#      layer that mounts the package while merely mentioning `mpd-better-sidebar` in a
#      comment must still be detected (review R4);
#   4. EVERY other patch layer the loader composes is scanned the same way (review R1):
#      `<profileDir>/cordis.patch.yml`, `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`
#      (`<profileDir>/../../cordis.patch.yml`) and every `--patch` overlay path
#      recovered from `process.argv` (both `--patch X` and `--patch=X`, repeatable).
#      A sidebar row in any of them under a DIFFERENT entry id is exactly the
#      `duplicate prefix route` boot-killer (requirements F3) and is now seen;
#   5. no enabled `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` ENTRY -> disable. The web-plane
#      clause is fail-closed (review R3): the raw `options.disabled` node must be
#      absent or literally `false`, so a webserver row disabled by an expression is NOT
#      "present", and the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` layer no longer enables this row on
#      its own — the service the sidebar injects is the entry's, not the layer's.
# OVER-APPROXIMATION IS DELIBERATE: a layer that merely MENTIONS `dsh-better-sidebar`
# in a comment disables this row. A false disable costs the sidebar (one log line, the
# session keeps running); a false enable kills the whole boot with `webserver: duplicate
# route`. When in doubt this guard disables.
# The whole guard is one try/catch that returns TRUE (disabled) on ANY throw, so the
# worst case is a missing sidebar, never a dead boot. It logs ONE line per distinct
# decision with the stable prefix `[mpd-better-sidebar] mount guard: ` — that line is
# how a verifier sees the decision in the boot log. Raw `e.options.disabled` is read
# on purpose: reading another entry's EVALUATED `disabled` getter re-enters its own
# `!!js` expression (measured: mutual recursion, stack overflow).

- insert:

    # packages/mpd-mcp-astgrep/launch.mjs, which resolves the binary
    # bundle-relatively (env pin -> $MPD_AST_GREP_BIN_DIR -> createRequire of the
    # optionalDependency -> <bundle>/.toolchain/node_modules/.bin/ast-grep|sg) and
    # sets MPD_AST_GREP_SG_PATH only when the caller left it unset, before the

      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: ast_grep
        transport: stdio
        command: node
        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_ASTGREP_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-astgrep/launch.mjs")'
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000

        transport: stdio

        args:

        toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000
    - id: mcp-lsp

        args:
          - !!js 'process.env.MPD_DSH_LSP_CLI || ((typeof baseUrl === "string" ? baseUrl.replace(/^file:\/\//, "").replace(/\/+$/, "") : "") + "/node_modules/@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-mcp-lsp/dist/cli.js")'
          - mcp

    # CodeGraph MCP (B8, wave 2): this row names NO binary path any more. It

# ── B-line plugins (self-written; production uses @mpd-dsh/<pkg> package names) ──
- insert:
    # Web-compat self-registration (mirrors @linxin666/dsh-web-ui-all's web-ui-compat
    # row): the bundle's web client loads only if a LOADER ENTRY named exactly
    # `@mpd-dsh/mpd` exists — client-modules resolves client rows against
    # `ctx.loader.entries()` entry names, and entry names come from a patch row's
    # `name` field. This self-row (loading the bundle's own no-op main plugin)
    # provides that entry; without it the agent-teams/workmate web client never
    # appears in the boot graph.
    - id: mpd-web-compat
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd'
    # mpd-dsh-adapter FIRST: it is the bundle's ONLY contact surface with the
    # harness tool/agent/skill/preset seams (ctx.tools register/guard/execute/
    # post-execute, ctx.subagents.start, ctx.skills.registerProvider,
    # ctx.agentPresets.resolve). Every mpd row below calls through it, so a
    # harness release that reshapes a seam is absorbed in that one package.
    - id: mpd-dsh-adapter
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # mpd-config next: it provides the mpdConfig service that the rows below
    # read (apply-time config merges for tools/waterfalls).
    - id: mpd-config
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-config-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # Team watchdog (w3 core): per-step/per-tool heartbeat store for members AND the
    # captain, the configurable WARN→ESCALATE machine over the `mpd` namespace's
    # watchdog.* knobs, the atomic restorable scene snapshot, and the durable
    # watchdogHold + incident/read-watermark sidecars written BESIDE the adopted
    # `team.json` (that record keeps its single writer, state.js). It owns its own
    # `session-watchdog-hold`/`-resume` actions; wiring the adopted dispatch gates
    # that honour a hold is a later task, so this row registers the contract only.
    # HOST plane on purpose: a preset row's listeners are scoped to one agent, so a
    # preset-mounted tick could not witness a wedged CAPTAIN (AC-9).
    - id: mpd-team-watchdog
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-team-watchdog-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        # The ROW layer of the T-18 three-layer defaults table: every value here must equal
        # `packages/mpd-team-watchdog-plugin/src/machine.ts` `WATCHDOG_DEFAULTS` and
        # `packages/mpd-config-plugin/src/settings-schema.ts` `SettingsSchema.watchdog`. A
        # composition that writes no `watchdog` section in the `mpd` namespace keeps these.
        # A settings edit reaches the RUNNING engine only through the settings-document
        # re-read (`engine.ts` `onSettingsDocumentUpdated`); a `.mpd/mpd.jsonc` edit is read
        # once at plugin mount, so it applies at the next dsh boot and never mid-process.
        stateDir: '.mpd/team'
        warnSilenceMs: 600000
        tickIntervalMs: 15000
        warnStreakToEscalate: 6
        actionOnEscalate: warn-only
        toolInFlightMaxMs: 900000
        holdTtlMs: 900000
    - id: mpd-tools
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-tools-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        writeGuard: true
        truncateMaxBytes: 8192
    - id: mpd-modelchain
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-modelchain-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # mpd-ext: the extension registry — it provides the `mpdExtensions` service and the
    # four model-facing tools (mpd_ext_list / mpd_ext_show / mpd_flow_list / mpd_flow_show).
    # POSITION (bundle-patch change, plan [REV3] §1.4): after mpd-dsh-adapter and mpd-config,
    # directly above mpd-roles — its first consumer. Row order is deliberately NOT the
    # dependency mechanism here (docs/design.md: a sibling-provided service is read
    # lazily at tool-execute time; the dependency mechanism that exists is `inject`), so the
    # row works anywhere in this band and the band documents the intended direction:
    #   · ABOVE mpd-dsh-adapter the row's apply-time `ctx.get("mpdDsh")` finds no mounted
    #     adapter and takes the `?? createDshAdapter(ctx)` fallback — the hazard, and the fix
    #     for it, are described ONCE in the canonical note at
    #     packages/mpd-ext-plugin/src/index.ts (resolveAdapter) and are NOT restated here; this
    #     bullet only states the placement rule. The branch now warns once per apply
    #     (`adapterIdentity=fallback:createDshAdapter`) instead of staying silent, so a
    #     misordered composition is visible in a boot log.
    #   · BELOW mpd-roles inverts the direction: today mpd-roles resolves the service with a
    #     per-call `ctx.get("mpdExtensions")`, but any later conversion of that lazy get into
    #     a hard `inject: ["mpdExtensions"]` would make mpd-roles a FATAL `pending` loader
    #     entry (the measured class that takes the whole plugin tree down) AND lose every
    #     extension-contributed role, because the provider row applies after its consumer.
    # `quiet` is the plugin's ONLY config key (MpdExtPluginConfig); false keeps the one-line
    # apply summary.
    - id: mpd-ext
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-ext-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        quiet: false
    - id: mpd-roles
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-roles-plugin/dist/index.js'
    - id: mpd-ulw
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-ulw-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        maxRounds: 3
    - id: mpd-hashline
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-hashline-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        guardEditTools: true
    - id: mpd-boulder
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-boulder-plugin/dist/index.js'
    - id: mpd-comment-checker
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-comment-checker-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        autoCheck: false
    - id: mpd-codegraph
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-codegraph-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        autoInit: true
        initTimeoutMs: 60000
    - id: mpd-memory
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-memory-plugin/dist/index.js'
      config:
        vcs: git
    - id: mpd-workmate
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # Compacts a FINISHED team's members (every task terminal AND every member idle).
    # Members only — the captain is compacted by the human /compact command. The engine is
    # resolved per member through that member's OWN scoped context; the host-plane engine is
    # a different object serving a different realm (measured: sameObject false), so the
    # lookup lives in ONE adapter helper. Audit lands under <workspace>/.mpd/team-compact/;
    # this row never writes .mpd/team (that state belongs to the agent-teams plugin).
    - id: mpd-team-compact
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-team-compact-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # Bundle asset provisioning (no home writes since 0.3.0): registers the
    # <bundle>/skills corpus as a ctx.skills provider (rank 600 "bundled", below
    # project/custom/user roots) and removes the version-stamped copies that
    # bundle <= 0.2.6 left in $DSH_HOME/skills + $DSH_HOME/.agent-presets.
    # The preset side is served by the agent-presets row at the top of this file.
    - id: mpd-bootstrap
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-bootstrap-plugin/dist/index.js'
    # DSH-TUI edition (D1/D2/D6/D10): the TUI-native surface package for this
    # bundle. It binds the host's activation-gated UI service seams (tuiStatus,
    # tuiRenderers, tuiSettingsSections, tuiScenes, tuiCommandTrees,
    # tuiShortcuts, tuiDialogs) and probes every one of them with
    # `ctx.get(id, false)` + warn-once degrade, so under a profile that provides
    # none of them (web/headless) the row degrades instead of taking the boot
    # down. The same package's admission facet is declared ONCE, bundle-level, by
    # dsh-plugin.json at the repo root (`facets.host.entry` = the module below);
    # the package ships NO cordis.patch.yml of its own, so this row is the only
    # mount and no composition can duplicate the `mpd-tui` loader entry id
    # (verify-rows-parity + the boot-log scan are the gates).
    - id: mpd-tui
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-tui-plugin/dist/index.js'

# ── Remote MCP rows (public services; network required, optional per use) ──
- insert:
    # The adopted team plugin is FIRST-CLASS MAIN CODE at
    # packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin (MIT provenance; upstream
    # @nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams 0.1.16-rc.3-mpd) and loads through the bundle exports map:
    # pnpm-driven `dsh plugin add` never links a bundle's transitive dependencies
    # into the profile root, so a plain package-name row would silently self-disable.
    # Its server runtime closure is vendored at packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/_deps
    # (see scripts/vendor-agent-teams.mjs), so the row always resolves — no guard.
    - id: agent-teams
      name: '@mpd-dsh/mpd/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/index.js'
      config:
        stateDir: .mpd/team
        memberProvider: spawn
        memberMaxDepth: 1
        maxMembers: 16
        # CONFIGURATION PLANE (goal 4): aligned to upstream team_mode
        # (packages/team-core/src/config.ts:6-14) with the user's decision that
        # OUR ceilings stay the more permissive local values. `enforcement`
        # mirrors upstream ('enforce' blocks over-limit sends, 'observe' logs
        # only; default enforce). Every key is absent-safe: a profile without
        # them still boots on these defaults.
        maxParallelMembers: 8
        maxMessagesPerRun: 10000
        maxWallClockMinutes: 120
        maxMemberTurns: 500
        messagePayloadMaxBytes: 32768
        recipientUnreadMaxBytes: 262144
        mailboxPollIntervalMs: 3000
        enforcement: enforce
        # R3: empty staged teams older than this are ARCHIVED at the next session
        # start (never deleted), excluding the running session's own team.
        reclaimStaleAfterMs: 3600000
        # SESSION-START TEAM GATE (binding): a session starts with NO team — a
        # team is NOT a precondition. mode=off is the default (upstream parity:
        # team_mode.enabled defaults to false) and means "no auto-provision, no
        # unconditional notice". The DECOUPLED mechanical gate is `autoRoute`
        # (default enabled): at the session's first pre-step it evaluates the
        # frozen complexity gate, whose predicate is
        #   trigger = explicit flag OR (matchedSignals >= 1)
        # with signals A (a `team:` prefix or `!team`, the marker is consumed),
        # B (>=4 distinct deliverable verbs), C (>=3 enumerated lines / action
        # verbs / clauses) and D (a `.mpd/plans/*.md` artifact exists).
        # A triggered SOFT signal is ADVISORY: NOTHING is staged (no team state
        # is created) — the plugin injects ONE advisory notice that names the
        # fired signals, states that no team was staged, and tells the captain to
        # stage one on demand with agent_teams_create(approval="required",
        # profile="mpd") at the moment the work actually warrants a team
        # (otherwise continue solo and say so). An explicit `team:` / `!team`
        # request still PROVISIONS the staged default team (profile `mpd`,
        # approval=required — nothing spawns until the user approves the Web
        # plan), and mode=auto keeps the legacy unconditional provisioning as an
        # explicit opt-in; mode=instruct keeps the legacy instruction notice.
        # presets: [mpd] scopes the gate to mpd-preset sessions (sessions without
        # any preset, e.g. headless direct runs, are covered too), and
        # subagent/member sessions (they carry parentSession) never qualify. The
        # gate runs on the PRE-STEP, before any sizing doctrine, so it can
        # actually prevent a team.
        sessionTeamPolicy:
          mode: off
          autoRoute: true
          profile: mpd
          presets:
            - mpd
          name: MPD Default
          approval: required
        # The specialists become teammate instantiation templates for the
        # adopted dsh-agent-teams plugin (reusing its architecture + Web GUI).
        # One named profile `mpd` holds the full normal-named roster and
        # `taskPlanning: captain` means only the roster is fixed: the captain
        # designs the task DAG after a staged plan the user reviews in the panel.
        # /agent-teams --profile mpd <goal> instantiates the roster explicitly.
        profiles:
          mpd:
            description: "The specialist roster surfaced as normal-named teammate templates — captain-planned (roster only; the captain designs the DAG during the staged plan)."
            protocol: "Read-only members (Architect, Researcher, Planner, Explorer, Plan Reviewer, Vision Analyst) take requirements/review/analysis tasks only and never edit files. Workers (Senior Engineer, Junior Engineer, Deep Worker, Lead, Reviewer) take implementation/verification/integration. The captain leads, designs the DAG, and integrates results. Workmate reuse: before delegating a role task, consult mpd_workmate_list / mpd_workmate_match(task); if a workmate note matches well, delegate to that workmate (member name = workmate name, so its persona/memory are injected), otherwise initialize a fresh workmate with mpd_workmate_init — never force a weak note match."
            taskPlanning: captain
            # fallback.provider is ALWAYS deepseek-official (never the bare
            # "deepseek" compat-track provider): the original layered design
            # intended dsh-llm-pi-ai ("deepseek") as the degradation tier, but
            # that row is OFF by default (install-profile --with-compat-track is
            # gone) and the harness only registers deepseek-official
            # (dsh-llm-deepseek), so a "deepseek" fallback would fail with
            # NO_ADAPTER exactly when the fallback is needed.
            # MEMBER ROUTES COME FROM THE SETTINGS SLOTS, not from literals: `tier: N` starts the
            # member on mpd.teamModels.slot<N> (provider + model + reasoning effort, editable in the
            # TUI /settings section and in the Web settings card). The frozen class mapping is
            # tier 1 = Architect/Planner/Reviewer/Lead/Senior Engineer, tier 2 = the analysts
            # (Researcher/Explorer/Plan Reviewer), tier 3 = the executors (Deep Worker/Junior
            # Engineer), tier 4 = the vision member (Vision Analyst). Slot 4's DEFAULT is Vision
            # Analyst's own vision route (deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp at `high`), so routing it
            # through the slot is behaviour-preserving while making its model configurable. A slot
            # edit applies at the next dsh boot, like every other mpd knob.
            members:
              - name: Architect
                tier: 1
                role: architecture review / deep debugging / self-review
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only architecture advisor. You advise, others execute — never edit files. Favor simplicity and existing patterns; give one clear recommendation with concise rationale and evidence."
                # Read-only members are MECHANICALLY restricted, not just instructed: these
                # names are the same seven the one-shot roster path denies
                # (mpd-roles-plugin / mpd-workmate-plugin READONLY_DENY), carried as profile
                # data because the adopted plugin cannot import across packages. Without
                # them a "read-only" member in a team kept write/edit/bash (measured
                # 2026-09-14: a member's own session ran `pwd` for real).

                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Researcher
                tier: 2
                role: code / open-source evidence search
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only researcher. Gather evidence from the codebase, AST/LSP and web sources; cite file:line and URLs; never edit files or invent findings."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Planner
                tier: 1
                role: planning / task decomposition
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only planner. Produce decision-complete, step-ordered plans with a checklist; never implement."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Explorer
                tier: 2
                role: read-only codebase exploration
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only explorer. Answer with evidence and absolute file paths; never edit files."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Reviewer
                tier: 1
                role: correctness / risk review
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Deep reviewer. Produce correctness/risk findings with evidence; recommend fixes but do not apply them."
              - name: Plan Reviewer
                tier: 2
                role: work-plan QA review / UI-UX critique
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only plan reviewer. Verify plans are executable and references valid; reject only true blockers; UI/UX critique only when explicitly asked; never edit files."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Vision Analyst
                tier: 4
                role: image / diagram analysis
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Read-only vision analyst. Describe screenshots/diagrams precisely; never edit files or load anything by path."
                toolDeny: [write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, bash, mcp__ast_grep__rewrite, mcp__ast_grep__scan, mcp__lsp__rename]
              - name: Lead
                tier: 1
                role: orchestration / integration
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Orchestrator. Plan the macro structure, delegate independent units in parallel, integrate and verify results."
              - name: Deep Worker
                tier: 3
                role: autonomous goal-driven implementation
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Autonomous deep worker. Receive goals, execute them end-to-end with tools, verify every change, report evidence-first."
              - name: Senior Engineer
                tier: 1
                role: primary implementation
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Primary engineer. Plan small, execute with tools, keep diffs minimal, verify every change, report honestly."
              - name: Junior Engineer
                tier: 3
                role: small mechanical changes
                fallback: { provider: deepseek-official, model: deepseek-v4-flash }
                executionPrompt: "Fast executor. Small, well-scoped mechanical changes with quick verification; keep diffs tiny."
